issues.description: Symbol 'display_start' is treated inconsistently: the problem statement and the template/main use 'display_start' as the base address of the framebuffer (an address/label to be added to an offset). The solution's set_pixel implementation computes an offset in EAX and then does 'add eax, [display_start]' which dereferences the memory at display_start (reads the dword stored at that address) instead of adding the symbol address. This causes the computed address to be wrong and the pixel write to target an incorrect location, confusing students about whether display_start is an address or stored data.
issues.suggestedFix: Treat 'display_start' consistently as the base address. In the solution's set_pixel replace 'add eax, [display_start]' with either 'add eax, display_start' (add the symbol address) or use 'mov esi, display_start' then add the computed offset to ESI and write with 'mov [esi], ecx'. Ensure the same address-vs-content convention is used in main and set_pixel.
